title: Section 80C Deductions under Income Tax Act
source: Income Tax Department, Government of India (Income Tax Act 1961 & Income Tax Act 2025)
reference: Section 80C, Income Tax Act 1961 — recodified as Section 123 under Income Tax Act 2025
content: Section 80C of the Income Tax Act 1961 (recodified as Section 123 under the Income Tax Act 2025) allows individual taxpayers and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) to claim deductions up to ₹1,50,000 per financial year from their gross total income. Permissible investments and expenses under Section 80C (Section 123) include: Employee Provident Fund (EPF), Public Provident Fund (PPF), Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS mutual funds), National Savings Certificate (NSC), Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY), 5-year Fixed Deposits with scheduled banks, Principal repayment of housing loans, Tuition fees paid for up to two children, and Life Insurance Premiums paid for self, spouse, or children. Note: Section 80C (Section 123) deductions are only available under the Old Tax Regime. They cannot be claimed under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC / Section 202).
